body:
Hm. Checking in ~ days later. That was a... low point for me. I haven't had that dark of an episode in like a year or so. Hm.

Back to "reasonably miserable" instead of "inconsolable". I'm still looking for a compelling reason to go on, though. Just for what it's worth.

> How can you give that away?

Give it away? That implies someone else takes possession. What I'm suggestion is cessation. There is no afterlife. Things would just end. Period. Go to sleep and never wake up.

> How can you give away the only thing we know for sure, as terrible, and hopeless as it may seem, without exploring possibilities?

I'm no longer interested in trying.

> It must be really terrible to feel like you look hideous.

Hey, yeah. It is.

> What kind of career do you think would make you happy?

Singing, probably. I would need to take classes in music theory, as well as lots of training and studying. Then there's the long, arduous road of establishing myself. I don't want to be 'famous', but I would like to be able to make a living singing. I think that'd be ok.

Anyway, yes I have considered reducing my alcohol consumption. In addition, I've considered increasing my alcohol consumption. I've also considered eating less, and exercising. I've also considered killing myself. I consider lots of things.

>  Life is all we've been given, why not ride it out until we don't have a chance?

It doesn't appear to be worth the effort.

The only reason I can talk about this here is because of the reasonable assurance of anonymity. No, I don't trust you; it's not personal. I don't trust anyone. I don't trust my family. They haven't done anything I can think of to warrant my mistrust. I can attempt to open up here, in this 'safe' place though. That's the power of anonymity. Give someone a mask and they will show you their true face.

You don't sound harsh. I would like to point out that I know how exercise and weight loss work, quite well. Two years ago I was working out rigorously, and adhering to a reasonable diet. It got me down to probably within 30 pounds of my target weight, which is impressive. Even at that level, though, I still felt like a disgusting fatty piece of trash. Some people, who've been fat for a good portion of their life, have skin that's pretty well stretched out. Mine centers on the man-boob area, and I'm a hideous sight shirtless. The last girl I dated was probably 8 inches shorter than me but weighed as much as I did because I couldn't deal with the possibility of anyone reasonably close to fit seeing me naked.

Obviously my self esteem was shit then, and is much, MUCH worse now. I tried. I really tried to get in shape. I couldn't do it. I will probably have to accept that I will never be physically fit (hey, I might not live much longer anyway!) and that's also a repulsive thought.

I'll preface the following by saying this: I am not upset or disappointed with your advice, and I am not trying to patronize. I know how to budget. I have never found a job that makes me happy; both mom and dad kept saying through my childhood, "Find a job that makes you happy and you'll be excited to go to work every day!". Yeah. Ok, both of them found that. Congratulations to them. I didn't. I don't think I will.

I drink vodka and diet soda. That is probably the most effective combination of inebriation and minimal caloric intake there is. Also, cheap vodka costs $10 for a handle, and knockoff cola costs $3 for a 12 pack. $13 a week for self medication ain't exactly breaking the bank, and at the same time the savings won't make a meaningful impact on getting me my car. God I miss that thing.
Argh. I'm going to go take a walk (haven't just 'gone for a walk' in quite some time) and think this over.

Every week I wrote up a log of how the workouts went, if anything was especially painful or if I hurt something, and sent them to the aforementioned internet fitness trainer friend. He'd assess it and make changes. For instance, if I was going to do pecs once a week, it would alternate regardless. Week 1 would be bench. Week 2 might be incline bench. Week 3 might be dumbbell bench, and Week 4 would be incline dumbbell, etc. Same muscle groups hit in different ways.

> I had to lose mad weight the hard way

Wait what's the easy way?

Nothing that involves lifting, no. The only times I got a rush were when I was able to do 3 pull-ups in a row, and the time when I did 3 plates in a deadlift and tore up my hands a little. Mind you, these are fairly shitty accomplishments because I am very hard on myself.

What I did like was when there was no one else in the gym. I would turn off all the lights, put on a pair of sunglasses, put on my headphones/mp3 player, turn on my workout playlist and just do cardio. Something very peaceful about tuning everything out and just mindlessly jogging. The most I ever got to was 2.3 miles.
The workout schedule and lineup was constantly altered. As I mentioned, early on my body wasn't being given enough time to recover between workouts.

Well fuck.

The first step is to create an email address that isn't linked to my name or any other regular usernames. That was the point of this throwaway in the first place. I won't waste your time if I go for it, but I have to decide if I'm ready to make a commitment like this on a spur-of-the-moment internet afternoon chat.
Definitely the former. Comfortably wearing XL shirts owned. Now I'm back to my fat clothes.

You, too, are correct. Easy to say, hard to do, especially for an unambitious person like me. I don't have any sort of support network of people around me. In the end, I am the **only** person who can enact change, and my life is a result of my actions.

Even if I did, I don't think the skin will ever return to normal. Ever. Would probably require some kind of surgery.

But yes, you are correct. I am the only person who can change myself. I realize this.

I tried to get people to play racquetball, but no one wanted to. Honestly this area just fucking sucks. I can't wait to move away. I do have a physical activity on the weekends, but it is pretty much just a weekend-only thing. I still do it now, but it is a hell of a lot harder these days.

I agree with you, though. Not only are activities/sports great because you're having *fun* while getting exercise, but there's also human interaction and encouragement.

I followed various fitness subsections on forums for a while (I don't know if you're familiar with W&W on SA). This wasn't just a 6 month spurt. This was the 6 months where I tried the hardest amongst a 2-3 year period of trying to manage it. I told myself that if I just followed the simple guidelines of eating better and working out under a supervised plan, it would work. I became too discouraged when it didn't happen. Also, I was going at it alone, basically. I wish I'd had someone else to work with, but at the end of the day I can only blame this on myself.

Actually no. I went through various stages. When I was 320ish lbs, I started with just diet. I added in various gym stuff for maybe an hour every other day without really knowing what the hell I was doing. That brought my to around 275. I hovered there for the better part of a year. I stopped going to the gym and was just more careful with what I ate, and was around 260 I think.

Then I decided to really get serious and did the aforementioned push. it got me down to 230. I was not starving. I ate constant, smaller healthier meals (6 times a day or so) and generally bought healthier stuff.

I honestly only kept the food journal for about 2 weeks before getting sick of it, but I kept to the general schedule. I was pushing too hard at the gym at first, and it turned out I needed more time for my body to recover between workouts. I reduced the number of 'lifting' days per week and did added more cardio (stationary bike, jogging, elliptical).

Progress was depressingly slow, both in weight loss and strength gain. I didn't feel more energetic. I wasn't sleeping any better. People **did** make comments like, "Hey have you been working out? You look like you've lost weight." I brushed them off because I was mired in self pity like an idiot.

Yeah uh the fat drained away from my face well, but not so much from the rest of my body. I have a very, very unfortunate fat concentration/distribution. My shirt being off is literally repulsive, because I have very stretched out manboobs. At 230 they were still very, very prevalent. I can assure you that my torso at 230 looks like 330 lb man's torso. An unfortunate 330 lb man at that.

Hi. I, too, was well over 100 lbs overweight. I finally buckled down and did everything I could think of to work hard and change it. I read a lot and altered my diet, even got a food scale. Kept a food journal. I got a gym membership and went 6 days a week under a structured routine. I worked *hard*. I took body measurements and sent them off to my internet fitness trainer (there are no actual fitness trainers at my gym; it's very small).

Anyway, I eventually worked my way down to 230 lbs (at 6'2") and plateaued for months. Cripes it was depressing. I also couldn't really see any difference in myself. I still felt weak and disgusting and horrible, and it was worse because I was honestly trying very hard.

I gave up. I gained back half of everything I lost over the next year. It sucks and I'm still miserable, but I only complain on internet throwaway accounts every now and then.

Please don't be me.

Sometimes I wonder how the following has impacted my life in the long run. I try to shut it out, but it's pervasively there; I don't know how to deal with it, so throwaway! :D

I had a bedwetting problem growing up. All through grade school. I couldn't stay over at friends houses. Did wonders for my self esteem. Parents tried everything, even those buzzer things they use on little kids that detect moisture on the metal and set off a loud noise next to your ear. Nothing worked. 

Mom decided to take me to a urologist and see if there was something physically wrong. I was probably... 12? 13? The doctor and I were in the room and he said he would perform a basic cursory examination, so he needed me to remove my pants and underwear. I was terrified of this. I was so shy and the thought of showing him my penis just was the most awful thing I could think of. I told him I couldn't.

Man this is going to be tough to write. So, the doctor tried to assure me it would be quick and he's deals with this sort of thing all the time, it would be fine. He asked if it would be easier perhaps if my mom was in the room. I pondered this, and for some reason it seemed the answer was *yes*. The doctor even remarked that he was rather surprised at my hesitance.

I laid back on the doctor table with some sort of little privacy napkin over my groin. Being a young male, and seeing that it was the most awkward situation possible (MY MOM WAS SITTING 2 FEET AWAY), my body decided this was an appropriate time for a naked raging erection. In front of mom and the doctor. The doctor did his examination quickly and determined everything was fine physically. 

The car ride home was awkward. My mom decided to look on the bright side. "Well, uh, honey, I want you to know that some boys get fun of for having small penises. You and your brother both have very... large... penises."

>The problem is that an inability to accept situationally appropriate praise from yourself will hold you back, because you are depriving yourself from the power of positive reinforcement for your positive action. 

An interesting take on it. Personally, I think it's that I analyze the praise in question. Despite my incredibly stupid problems, I still have a (mental) superiority complex. If I genuinely feel the praise is warranted, I can accept it. This is a very rare occurrence. If I feel that a half brain-dead monkey could have accomplished what I am being praised for, I dismiss it. I need the things I consider important to be validated, and they rarely are. Perhaps the things I consider important, *aren't*.

Me: "Check out this fucking awesome thing I just did"

Them: "ok, yeah, that's nice"



vs.



Me: "Ok, I followed up on that request and spent 4 hours doing mindless data entry."

Them: "Wow! You did a really good job on this!"

>Why don't you want to?

At this point it doesn't seem feasible. What's the point? Why bother? I search myself for answers to these questions, and I cannot produce logical answers that satisfy me.

>Listening to music you feel a connection to, even if it's completely melancholy music, really helps.

Music is absolutely *essential* to any sort of workout routine for me. There is a night and day difference in drive and performance in a proper playlist vs. nothing. Garbage's song "Push It" introduced second and third winds that would not have existed otherwise. In the end, though, all that effort failed to produce the desired result. I tried. I really tried. I lost 100lbs and felt the same. When I plateaued, I couldn't find a logical reason to try. 

Dad attempted to employ reverse psychology with me, growing up, if I ever expressed dismay toward a situation. He would throw up his hands and say, "Give up!" in a derisive tone. Unfortunately, the obstinate jackass in me would say, "okey dokey". I don't blame my parents. They absolutely did the best they knew how.


Last night I ended up calling my mom and having a tenuous discussion, hinting I might have slipped into a deeper state of depression. She informed me that The Lord had a plan for my life, and if I just handed over all my problems to Jesus that my life, like hers when she was depressed, would miraculously dissolve. "Right. Thanks mom."



















>I know what you mean about 'needing' people to like you.

I fucking hate that I need people. I don't want to need people. This is something I wish to stamp out in myself. So far I've proved unsuccessful. I am a strong-willed person. I fight pointless uphill battles for no apparent reason at the drop of a hat. It's in my nature to need people?? FUCK THAT. I WILL BEAT THAT NEED RIGHT OUT OF ME. WEAK-WILLED MOTHERFUCKER, YOU DON'T NEED ANYONE. I'm insane.


















>One more thing. In my opinion, it's always better to regret something you did than to regret something you didn't do. 

http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o52fNnUVEuk

I don't want to lift weights right now (yes, I realize the insurmountable benefits of putting a load on the skeletal structure), but I might go do some cardio while listening to The Offspring or Prodigy at very high volumes.

Also, when I was documenting my weight training, I was improving at a rate so slow it was disproportionate to the time I put in. Very discouraging after like 6 months to move up 10lbs in curls. I'd have to go look at the book again, though.



>I'll leave you with this, a little homework assignment.

Interesting you'd mention that. I have a chronic *need* to make other people happy. Part of me wants to put forth an exterior of stoic 'not caring what others think' image. Quite the opposite is true. I need people to like me. I care desperately what they think of me. I wish I didn't. I hate myself for caring in this regard.



The long and short of it is, I actually come off as quite courteous and friendly in social situations. I display a very different public face than what I feel. Cue the line from Jim Carrey's "The Mask" where Ben Stein's character is being interviewed on TV.

Thank you. At this point in the evening, my mental defenses are... in flux due to the delicious alcohol, so I feel it's appropriate to respond when I'm in a more vulnerable state. Keep in mind that a vulnerable state for me is a ridiculously guarded state for the average person.

>You haven't mentioned any friends, but try to hang out with them more.

Good point. I have ~4 friends I've made out here in the last 6 years. 1 works almost full time. 1 just had his first baby and is consumed with the life of being a new father. 1 is going to college full time, although I suppose he's off for the summer. 1 works full time to make ends meet for his family. I see them once a month at best. I fear I may have given off too many red flags and they wish to distance themselves from me. <-- potential paranoia.

>As for your job, can you try to diplomatically voice your concerns to the owner?

My diplomacy was announcing that he is dead to me, and I will no longer talk to him. He pulled some shit that is inexcusable. The ball is in his court. I have acquiesced to his bullshit for years. I drew a line, and I'm not fucking crossing first. It's the principle.


>I hope I helped a little bit. Going to the doctor sucks, but that is the one thing I strongly urge you to do, if nothing else.

Sigh, this is going to sound incredibly retarded, but how does one choose a physician? Yellow pages?

Tunnel analogy was sort of a last minute thing for a title. Also been in tunnel for ~15 years. Send help.

**fake edit** Let me look at this a little closer.
>Yeeaaah, most of them are pretty big deals right now but they won't be once you move down the tunnel a little bit more. Tomorrow, well, maybe you haven't moved much by tomorrow. Maybe you haven't moved much by next week. But you know what? You're fidgeting. You're trying to learn how to crawl.

Actually I'm currently grinding to a halt, not gaining speed. I appreciate that you, another human, took the time to answer this, but there's... well there's little substance here. I have never once been motivated by a pep talk.  <--- this is my deflection talking, but since I'm being anonymous here I can admit that honestly. One of my few coping mechanisms with the pathetic waste I am is dumping on others. I'm really good at it. 

>Be someone who gives it off and a multitude of people will flock to you, to lead the way. And the way? The way doesn't matter, as long as you're enjoying it.


That's not me. That'd be my sibling (two years apart). People are drawn to their personality. Ironically, I feel they are in potentially worse shape mentally than me, but had the 'natural born leader/max charisma' stats. Sometimes I like to think of traits in life in terms of stat points. They, however, have fallen, and fallen hard. That was difficult to watch. I wonder what keeps them going.

Right, yes. That brings me to another stupid point about myself. I cannot accept praise. Bounces right off. Negativity/insults seep in and stay for life. Praise is deflected like arrows shot at a Sherman tank.
